framing.lineOfInquiry: Vivek Rawat (P00286) may have been involved in the incident recorded in CASE014
framing.alternate: Vivek Rawat (P00286) was not involved — the evidence has an innocent explanation
framing.note: KRONOS starts from the presumption of innocence. The line of inquiry and the alternates are tested against the same records; neither is a finding, and the strengths are not probabilities.

alternateHypotheses.title: Someone else used the phone or handset
alternateHypotheses.statement: Some records attributed to Vivek Rawat were generated by another person using the same phone or handset.
alternateHypotheses.label: Strong

evidence.text: Handset IMEI-355623920908551 is also used by P00308 — another person may have generated some records
Shares a handset with P00308 but is a different person (household or shared device)

alternateHypotheses.test: Handset forensics and SIM CAF/KYC; establish who carried the handset at the incident time (the other user's location, CCTV).

alternateHypotheses.title: Named or given a role in error
alternateHypotheses.statement: Vivek Rawat was named in the FIR, or assigned a role, without an independent basis.
alternateHypotheses.label: Moderate

evidence.text: FIR text contains: '…no role has been attributed…'

alternateHypotheses.test: Re-examine the FIR and statements; record the person's statement and the informant's basis for naming them.

alternateHypotheses.title: The money has a legitimate explanation
alternateHypotheses.statement: The flagged money movements of Vivek Rawat have an ordinary purpose (salary, rent, property, business) or belong to a co-holder of the account.
alternateHypotheses.label: Moderate

evidence.text: Flagged NEFT ₹720,000 on 2025-03-09 17:16 has a stated purpose 'consultancy fee'

alternateHypotheses.test: Obtain full statements, invoices or agreements and KYC; confirm the stated purpose with the counter-party.

alternateHypotheses.title: The contact was routine, not coordination
alternateHypotheses.statement: Vivek Rawat's calls and messages reflect a long-standing relationship (family, work, business), not planning of the incident.
alternateHypotheses.label: Weak

evidence.text: In contact with Arjun Bhatia since 2025-02-11, 26 days before the incident (6 calls, 8 messages) — a long-standing relationship
In contact with Manisha Gupta since 2025-02-10, 26 days before the incident (8 calls, 3 messages) — a long-standing relationship

alternateHypotheses.test: Examine message content and the timing of contact relative to the incident; establish the relationship.

alternateHypotheses.title: Was near the scene for a routine reason
alternateHypotheses.statement: Vivek Rawat was near the scene because they regularly go there (home, work, market), not because of the incident.
alternateHypotheses.label: Weak

evidence.text: Recorded within 1 km of the scene on 39 other days (07 Feb – 07 Apr), so presence there is part of their routine

alternateHypotheses.test: Establish why the person is regularly there (address, employment, shop) and compare the incident-time visit with their usual pattern (time of day, duration).

comparison.verdict: Every supporting item could be explained by at least one alternate, although the line of inquiry is stronger on weight (0.84 vs 0.72). Test the alternates before relying on it.
settleWith: A3 — Handset forensics and SIM CAF/KYC; establish who carried the handset at the incident time (the other user's location, CCTV).
A6 — Re-examine the FIR and statements; record the person's statement and the informant's basis for naming them.
A4 — Obtain full statements, invoices or agreements and KYC; confirm the stated purpose with the counter-party.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Vivek Rawat (P00286) was involved in the incident recorded in CASE014
hypotheses.name: Vivek Rawat

alternativeExplanations: Being named in an FIR records an allegation; it is not itself proof of involvement.
Flagged transactions may have legitimate explanations (business payments, loans, property, salary) — verify documents.
Frequent contact may reflect family, business or social ties unrelated to the incident.

confidence.note: Evidential balance compares weighted supporting vs contradicting evidence; it is not a probability of guilt. Prior records are excluded from this score.

note: Each hypothesis is tested from both sides to reduce confirmation bias. Confidence scores are evidential balance (not probability of guilt). Human review is required.
